I’d fix these before merging. Reviewed `excerpt-helper` (`59856d7`) against `main`; no files changed.

1. **[P1] The helpers aren’t connected to card rendering.**  
   `src/card.js:1–2` still returns `entry.body.trim()`. Nothing calls `toPlain` or `excerpt`, so cards continue showing the full Markdown body. The branch adds helpers but doesn’t deliver the card-preview behavior.

2. **[P1] Short text gets truncated, and every result gets an ellipsis.**  
   `src/excerpt.js:6–8` always searches for a space and appends `…`, even when the input fits:
   - `excerpt('hello world', 20)` → `'hello…'`
   - `excerpt('', 20)` → `'…'`

   This contradicts the documented unchanged-input behavior. Check whether truncation is needed before finding a cut point.

3. **[P2] A word ending exactly at the limit is unnecessarily dropped.**  
   `src/words.js:2–3` excludes the character at index `limit` when searching for a space. For `excerpt('one two three', 7)`, the space immediately after `two` is a valid boundary, but the result is `'one…'` rather than `'one two…'`. The existing words test actually enshrines this off-by-one behavior.

4. **[P2] Markdown flattening deletes literal content and leaves markup behind.**  
   `src/plain.js:3–4` removes marker characters without considering their context:
   - `'snake_case'` → `'snakecase'`, despite the underscore being literal.
   - `'# Hello'` remains `'# Hello'`.
   - `'![photo](https://x)'` → `'!photo'`.
   - `'[link](https://example.com/a(b))'` → `'link)'`.

   A Markdown-aware conversion would avoid altering literal text and handle these valid constructs.

**Validation:** all four existing tests pass, but the edge-case checks above reproduce these problems. Coverage should include short/empty inputs, exact-limit boundaries, literal Markdown characters, and a card-level test exercising the full conversion path.
